paragraphs: Samsara sells a platform to organizations that run vehicles and equipment, pitched on improving safety, lowering costs and changing how operations work. For fleets it covers live GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, fuel analytics and compliance reporting. The company presents this as one platform working across every part of an operation rather than separate tools.

Its cameras pair safety detections with video that managers can pull on demand. The company says the system watches for drowsiness, distraction, tailgating and forward collision risk. It states that these are caught in real time and trigger an in-cab alert before a manager is involved. A multicamera option adds up to four auxiliary HD feeds for visibility around the vehicle. A separate site product brings third-party cameras at facilities into a cloud dashboard for onboarding and troubleshooting.

The camera pages list transportation and logistics, field services, construction, public sector and essential services among the industries served. For school districts the company describes arm-mounted cameras that enforce school bus stop-arm compliance during pickups and drop-offs. Among its customer stories is one saying the City of El Paso recovered $1.3M in assets and reduced accidents by 29%. A site camera gateway is listed as compliant with the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.
